Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, the fish-control transfer instructions, and both required wake views before proposing or editing the candidate. Then I’ll trace the assigned parent and sampled rollout evidence, implement one candidate only, and update both required reasoning files.

The workspace is a later Phase 2 iteration with four identical scored examples (`capture`, 0.7484 L minimum distance), and the prefilled solver is the assigned parent. I’m now applying the two relevant workspace skills: the bookshelf for mechanism transfer, and the visual-first protocol for interpreting the wake evidence before any architecture change.

All four sampled solvers are byte-identical replications of the same strong capture, so there is no sampled termination failure to compare. I’ll use the inherited step-27 regressive capture as the informative negative comparator, while retaining the older boundary-exit cases in inherited guidance as counterevidence. This satisfies the visual comparison without pretending a scalar tie contains distinct evidence.

The two views agree with the diagnostics: both policies self-propel along the same diagonal path, shed a compact alternating wake, and execute the same late hook; the posterior-only variant’s regression is too small to form a distinct visual route class. Because the inherited last three completed iterations are exact nominal repetitions with no new semantics, the structured protocol now requires a fresh bookshelf consultation; I’ll use it to screen for a genuinely different mechanism, not to justify gain tuning.

The shelf supports only one fresh mechanism that is compatible with this evidence: a terminal approach hold based on measured yaw/slip, because broad phase, rate, and authority reallocations are already falsified and no external wake disturbance exists to calibrate a residual. I’m auditing the current state-feedback path and terminal trace now to determine whether a strictly local, bounded damping veto has an evidenced sign and whether it can be made inactive on the far route.

The inherited optimizer samples add evidence the assigned parent has not yet distilled: posterior-only delivery, headroom transfer, and coupled anti-windup all preserve capture but worsen margin/mean distance or effort. I’m folding those completed negatives into the decision boundary. They make a speculative terminal yaw/slip layer unjustified here—the trace has rapidly oscillatory yaw, persistent slip, and no demonstrated actuator-to-slip sign—so the evidence favors preserving the proven controller and recording the stagnation boundary rather than manufacturing a new residual.

I’ve completed the pre-edit diagnosis. The candidate will remain the single evaluated v41 policy: four byte-identical nominal captures establish reproducibility, while every available terminal redistribution is negative and the shelf offers no calibrated new invariant for this still-water trace. I’m recording that selection now, then materially revising durable guidance so later workers stop spending nominal CFD on equivalent terminal allocators and instead require held-out evidence before reopening them.

The candidate decision is now complete: one active v41 policy is retained, and the durable guidance now incorporates the four exact nominal replications plus three completed joint-coupling negatives. I’m invoking the required no-CFD check runner next; if it finds a contract or guidance-semantic issue, I’ll repair it and rerun.

The configured runner was invoked, but its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` is unsupported on this ChatGPT account—the same infrastructure limitation recorded by prior workers. I’ll execute its three declared no-CFD checks separately and report their actual results; this keeps validation substantive despite the agent-launch failure.

The guidance check passed. The first contract-check attempt did not execute because I supplied a malformed solver working-directory path; this was an invocation error, not a policy failure. I’m rerunning the exact check from the correct directory.

All three declared no-CFD checks now pass: reusable-guidance semantics, finite two-joint policy output, and solver edit boundary. I’m doing the final deterministic schema/static audit and then will append the validation results to the provenance notes; no CFD will be run.

Produced exactly one active candidate: the evidence-backed v41 policy, retained byte-identical to four successful sampled rollouts.

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) includes visual diagnosis, hypothesis, bookshelf transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:203) now records nominal-repeatability limits and the completed joint-coupling negatives.

All no-CFD checks pass: guidance semantics, finite two-joint contract, parameter schema (`87/87` references resolved), and editable-boundary validation. The configured check-runner model was unavailable, so its commands were executed directly.
